title: Firefly: Illuminating Large-Scale Verified Tool-Call Data Generation from Real APIs
claim: A multi-stage pipeline turns real tool servers into verified training tasks, then uses them for stable offline reinforcement learning.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, stacked sub-boxes, arrows between stages and outputs
description: A wide three-column diagram with color-coded stages: blue 'MCP Server Collection', teal 'Task Synthesis', and orange 'Reinforcement Learning'. Each column holds white sub-boxes with small icons. Blue column: scraping a registry, filtering by criteria such as statelessness and schema clarity, and building a tool-call graph. Teal column: LLM exploration of the tool graph, task summarization from a chain of tool calls (A to B travel example), and a task validation checklist. Orange column: agent rollout steps (think, tool call, output) with a retrieval-augmented simulator and a match? decision diamond (yes returns recorded output, no generates simulated output), and a reward section ending in a binary reward and policy optimization. Each column ends in a colored output bar. Large arrows link the columns, and the eye starts at the top-left header.
caption: Overview of FIREFLY. The pipeline first collects real-world MCP servers, filters them for reproducible and benchmarkable tool use, and constructs a tool-call graph from tool schemas. It then explores valid tool chains and summarizes observed tool-call states into natural-language tasks with verified labels, followed by validation for task quality and reliability. Finally, we use the validated tasks and verified labels for reinforcement learning: to avoid unstable live MCP servers during rollout, we build a retrieval-augmented tool-call simulator that replays or simulates tool outputs offline, enabling stable RL training with binary rewards and improving tool-call ability.
abstract: Training tool-calling agents requires large-scale trajectory data with verifiable labels, yet existing approaches either synthesize environments that diverge from real API behavior or generate tasks without ground-truth outcomes for verification. We present FireFly, a pipeline for generating verified tool-call data from real-world MCP servers. Our key insight is to invert the standard synthesis pipeline: rather than generating tasks and hoping they are solvable, we first let a strong LLM explore real APIs along graph-guided DAG structures, then synthesize tasks backward from observed outcomes, guaranteeing label correctness by construction. To handle the scale of real-world tool spaces (${\sim}$1,000 tools), we build a pairwise tool graph and sample sub-DAGs to focus exploration on semantically coherent workflows. To address environment drift in live APIs, we construct a retrieval-augmented simulator that caches all exploration results and replays them during training and evaluation, enabling fully offline and reproducible RL. Applying this pipeline yields 5,144 verified tasks spanning 240 servers and 993 tools. A 4B-parameter model trained with GRPO on FireFly matches Claude Sonnet 4.6 on our held-out test set and shows improvements on multiple tool-calling benchmarks including Tau2-Bench, MCPMark, and MCP-Atlas.
